name: Netshoot
what_it_is: Netshoot is a Docker and Kubernetes network troubleshooting container that bundles 30+ networking tools (tcpdump, iperf3, nmap, scapy, and others) and leverages Linux network namespaces to run diagnostics inside a target container's or host's network namespace without modifying the production environment.
components: tshark / termshark — packet inspection with TUI
mtr — traceroute with continuous latency tracking
nmap / nping — port scanning and packet generation
drill / dig / nslookup — DNS query tools
netstat / ss — connection and routing visualization
ipset / ipvsadm — IP set and IPVS load-balancing inspection
zsh with oh-my-zsh, bash, vim, git
measurement: HTTP response time and percentile latency (fortio)
configuration: Network namespace target: container namespace (--net container:<name>), host namespace (--net host), or Kubernetes pod namespace
Privilege level: unprivileged for basic diagnostics, privileged / NET_ADMIN + NET_RAW capabilities for packet capture and namespace manipulation
Docker socket mount (/var/run/docker.sock) required for ctop
Host netns filesystem mount (/var/run/docker/netns) required for Docker network namespace inspection
Deployment mode: standalone Docker container, Kubernetes ephemeral container (kubectl debug), Kubernetes pod, or Kubernetes sidecar
modes: Interactive shell (zsh or bash) — direct access to all bundled tools
Single-command execution — invoke a specific tool as the container entrypoint command
Sidecar — long-running process sharing a pod's network namespace alongside an application container
Ephemeral debug container — attached to a running Kubernetes pod via kubectl debug
Batch capture — background tcpdump writing to file
Real-time monitoring — live metric observation via termshark, ctop, or iftop
constraints: Packet capture and namespace manipulation require privileged mode or NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW capabilities — cannot run these operations unprivileged
Docker network namespace inspection requires mounting the host's /var/run/docker/netns filesystem into the container
ctop requires access to the Docker socket (/var/run/docker.sock)
Read-only observation tool — cannot directly modify or remediate the target application or network configuration
Capture accuracy and throughput measurement are constrained by host interface capabilities and kernel version
No persistent storage, logging aggregation, or time-series retention — all data is ephemeral within the container session
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml is provided in the repository — it is a single-container image, not a multi-service stack
No automated remediation or self-healing capabilities
No GUI — only CLI and TUI interfaces
No built-in authentication or authorization beyond container-level isolation
No historical metric storage or time-series database integration
No service mesh deep inspection (e.g., Istio/Envoy control-plane visibility)
No application-level protocol stacks or server frameworks
